Every construction is a pure function of checked tables, so the `Machine` proofs\nand the Definition ID scheme carry over, and no behavior is defined outside a step function an\nauthor wrote (AUT-07a, AUT-09). The word is `compose`, not `system`: `system` is the reserved party\nfor the implementation under test (glossary Party) and the elaborator enforces it.\n\nVersion one composes only for `verify` Queries. No functional, canary, or exploratory set runs over\na composed Model, so the Producer, the realizations, Case production, Testpilot, every Case fixture,\nthe production canary's pinned Case identity, the recorded control Run, the exploration coverage\ngolden, and the replay bridge are unchanged: every committed fixture and golden is byte-identical\nafter this spec. The caller module stays where it is, and so do the Start and Outage entities: moving\nthe `operation` entity would rewrite every `temporal.nexus.caller.*` ID and re-pin the canary, and a\nshared `workflow` entity needs a key decision the grammar cannot express today (Start correlates by\n`firstExecutionRunId`, Outage by `workflowTaskCompletedEventId` because its only evidence carries no\nrun id). Both are recorded under Boundaries as the follow-up. Rule text that needs a\nGOV-02 draft is listed in Decision Context. The direction note `.plans/UMPIRE4_DIRECTION.md` and the\nconversation of 2026-09-26 record the reasoning.\n\n## Overview\n\nToday `Temporal.Feature` holds seven machines shaped around the upstream tests they replace, three\nof them copies of the Nexus reply logic, and no Property can relate a workflow to the worker that\nserves it or an operation to the worker that answers it. This spec gives the model a way to compose\nentities into one Model for cross-entity claims, adds the first entity module, and removes one of the\nthree copies. The full unification, which moves the operation entity, re-pins the canary, and needs\nan entity key that varies by use case, is named as the follow-up.\n\n## Goal & Context\n<!-- scope: business -->\n\nThe vision's first line is one model for software behavior. The tree has seven: `Workflow/Start` and\n`Workflow/Outage` each declare `entity workflow` with a different key and their own `startWorkflow`;\n`Nexus/Pair` and `Nexus/Control` copy the caller's reply logic over new phase enums; `System/Info`\nhas an `entity server` nothing else mentions. Only `Nexus/Caller` has the intended shape.\n\nThree structural causes: a machine tracks one entity and nothing composes machines of different\nentities; the search enumerates paths, so a composed state space was unaffordable before fn-88; and\nthe Case pipeline made the upstream test the unit of authoring. The concrete symptom this spec fixes\nfirst: `workerStop` is a stutter row on the operation machine, so the schedule-to-start timeout\nScenario orders the stop before the request by convention. With a worker machine composed in,\n`handlerReply` is enabled only while the worker polls, and that ordering becomes a checked fact.\n\nWho benefits: an author writing a cross-entity claim has a Model to write it against; the worker\nbecomes a first-class entity instead of a stutter row on two other machines; the Control model\nbecomes a visible one-row delta on the Pair machine instead of a third copy.\n\n## Architecture & Data Models\n<!-- scope: technical -->\n\n```text\nTemporal/Feature/\n  Worker/Model.lean        entity worker (key taskQueue), workerStop, workerResume, serve,\n                           machine polling                                                     new\n  Workflow/Outage/Model.lean unchanged; gains compose workerOutage (outage machine ∥ worker) and a\n                           cross-entity verify Query beside its functional set\n  Nexus/Caller/Model.lean  unchanged; gains machine handlerWorker (from: polling restrict:), compose\n                           nexusCaller (nexusProtocol ∥ handlerWorker), and a cross-entity verify\n                           Query beside the existing sets\n  Nexus/Control/Model.lean machine nexusControl from: pair extend: …, byte-identical Case        rewritten\n  Nexus/Pair, Nexus/Success, Workflow/Start, System/Info                                        unchanged\n```\n\nConstructions, all in `Umpire.Command`, all pure functions of checked tables:\n\n- **`compose` command.** Keys: `for:` the entities tracked; `state:` an author-written `structure`\n  with one field per member (field names are what predicates read; the structure derives no\n  `Finite`); `members:` one `field: machine` line per member;\n  `sync:` one line per synchronized action, `name: field.action ∥ field.action …`, naming which\n  member's action each participant is, first-named member's outcome reported; `starts:` and\n  `ends:` over the composed state, since members like the worker have no natural end. The command\n  generates `<name>.Action`, `<name>.Outcome`, and `<name>.Fact` as tagged unions with one\n  constructor per member wrapping that member's type, so catalog keys never collide and predicates\n  write `step.facts.contains (.operation .nexusOperationCompleted)`. Catalog keys obey\n  `FiniteCatalog.validKey` (alphanumerics, `-`, `_`), so an unsynchronized action is keyed\n  `<field>_<member key>` and a composed state `_`-joins its members' state keys in field order, the\n  spelling `instances:` already uses for `1_accepted` and its product states; a member field name\n  containing `_` is a located error. A synchronized action is keyed by its `sync:` name. Authors\n  refer to members with dots, `operation.handlerReply (async)`, and Scenario `actions:`, Scenario\n  `starts:`, and Property `when:` resolve those references and `sync:` names to the catalog keys,\n  so the elaborator's last-component action lookup and `-`-split phase lookup are extended for\n  compositions.\n  Semantics: an unsynchronized action steps its owner and leaves the others unchanged; a\n  synchronized step is enabled only when every participant has a row from its current state, and\n  its results are the ordered product of the participants' results, sorted by the existing step\n  order key, refused above 16 results with the counts; a participant may own a classless action\n  synchronized with a classed one, in which case its row applies to every class; two members\n  owning an action of the same name that no `sync:` line names is a located error; timers never\n  synchronize and are keyed per member.\n- **Reachable enumeration.** The composed table is built by a frontier breadth-first walk from the\n  composed start states through the members' tables, evaluated at elaboration and emitted as a\n  literal table. The state catalog is the reachable set sorted by lowered order key, as `instances:`\n  orders its catalogs, so the fingerprint is independent of discovery and member order. The bound\n  check is reachable states times actions against `enumerationBound`. An action never jointly\n  enabled is dropped from the catalog with a located warning. This walk is the command's own; the\n  literal is sorted by a total key before emission, since a stable sort would let ties carry the\n  `members:` order into the fingerprint.\n- **Composed state fields, starts, ends, timers.** The composed Model lowers every member's state\n  fields as its own state fields keyed `<field>_<memberField>` (a one-field member as `<field>`);\n  the member field itself is not a state field, because a whole-structure spelling would make every\n  nested predicate a disjunction the clause language refuses.\n- **Field-addressed requirements.** The `property` command's predicate enumeration fixes whole\n  states, outcomes, and facts today, so a claim on one member's field, `step.state.worker.phase ==\n  .polling` while the other member varies, fixes nothing and is refused. This spec adds one\n  requirement kind: a state field is fixed when every accepted step carries that field's value and\n  changing it to any other value of that field's catalog is rejected; it lowers to the same\n  transition-contract clause on the field's model value, which both the reference evaluator and the\n  Property monitors already match, because each offers a state's fields beside the state to a\n  resulting-state pattern. A claim that names every field of a unique composed state, as the\n  Outage claim can, is carried as a whole-state requirement without it. `starts:` and `ends:` on\n  `compose` name member-qualified values (`workflow.completed`); a composed state is terminal when\n  the named member field holds a listed value, and the machine rule that `ends:` values share one\n  carrying field does not apply. Each member's `timers:`, `unobservable:` entries, and `evidence:`\n  lines are lifted under `<field>.` keys; a `sync:` line naming a timer is a located error. A member\n  may itself refine another machine; the composition carries neither `refines:` nor an abstract\n  field.\n- **Search backend.** fn-88 is a dependency and closes before this spec starts: `Selection.select`\n  chooses the backend per Query with no author-facing override, `veil` when the Property lowers to\n  monitors and the Scenario is pinned, `reference` otherwise with a recorded reason, and\n  `Selection.cutover` is true. The two shipped claims are same-step `when:` Properties with a\n  state-field requirement over a `scenario` declaration, which lowers, so each runs on `veil` with\n  reason `default`; the kernel replay gate runs on every result as it does for every Query. The\n  backend differential is registry-driven and covers a Query once the module declaring it is\n  imported by the sweep module and its expected line is pinned, so every Query this spec declares,\n  fixture or shipped, is listed there.\n- **Proofs.** A generic theorem shows that a decidable check, `composedTableAgrees members literal\n  = true`, implies soundness and completeness of the literal with respect to the composition\n  function over reachable sources. The `compose` command emits that check for each composition by\n  `decide +kernel`, as the refinement decision does today, and refuses the composition with a located\n  error when it fails. The kernel time of that check and of the law proof is measured on both\n  shipped compositions, beside the predicate-enumeration seconds of their Properties. If either\n  exceeds the elaboration budget, the first fallback is a proof-shape change (per-row lemma\n  batching, `Nat` constructor-index comparisons instead of `String` equality inside the decided\n  `Bool`); `native_decide` comes only with the explicit policy approval `LEAN_GUIDELINES.md` §5\n  requires, recorded per module, and on Lean 4.32 it mints a per-call axiom rather than\n  `Lean.ofReduceBool`, so the R5 axiom pin fails on it by construction. `compose` elaborates to\n  `Umpire.Command.DeclaredModel` as `machine` does; a Query's `check` over it yields\n  `Umpire.Command.CheckedModel`, which still carries a `realizable` field as it does for every\n  `verify` Query, and nothing reads it because no set names a composition.\n- **`restrict:` and `extend:` on `machine`.** `machine x from: source restrict: [actions]` keeps only\n  the listed actions' rows and drops the rest from the catalog; `evidence:` lines for facts no\n  remaining row returns, `timers:` and `unobservable:` entries without rows are filtered. `extend:\n  action: step` appends the author's results to the named action's rows, with a located error for a\n  result at a source state where the action has no row and for a duplicate result; results are\n  sorted by the step order key. Both keys may appear on one machine; `restrict:` applies first. A\n  derived machine inherits neither `refines:` nor the abstract state field. `Nexus/Control` becomes\n  `from: pair extend: handlerReply: forgedStep` with the machine name, catalog keys, and result order\n  it has today, so its Case fixture and the recorded control Run under `tools/umpire/replay/testdata`\n  stay byte-identical; a derived machine re-owns its catalogs under its own namespace.\n- **Entity module.** `Worker/Model.lean` declares `entity worker` keyed by task queue, with\n  `workerStop`, `workerResume`, a classless `serve` action (a polling worker serves; a stopped one\n  has no row), and machine `polling` with `starts: [polling]` and `ends: [polling, stopped]`. The\n  handler's task-queue worker and the workflow's task-queue worker are two instances of this entity,\n  named by the member field of the composition that uses them. The caller and Outage modules keep\n  their own `workerStop` actions in version one; the compositions synchronize with them by name.\n- **Two compositions.** `workerOutage` composes `workflowOutage ∥ worker` with `sync: workerStop:\n  workflow.workerStop ∥ worker.workerStop`, `workerResume` likewise, and `awaitCompletion:\n  workflow.awaitCompletion ∥ worker.serve`, and verifies that a stopped worker completes no\n  workflow, as a claim on the unique composed state a completion leaves. `nexusCaller` composes\n  `operation ∥ handlerWorker`, where `handlerWorker` is `from: polling restrict: [workerStop,\n  serve]` declared in the caller module, with `sync: workerStop: operation.workerStop ∥\n  worker.workerStop` and `handlerReply: operation.handlerReply ∥ worker.serve`, and verifies with a\n  bare `when: handlerReply`, which covers every reply class, and a field-addressed requirement that\n  `handlerReply` never fires while the worker is stopped. The restriction is what keeps\n  `workerResume` out of that composition; composing the full `polling` machine would admit a\n  stop-resume-reply path the boundary excludes. The Outage functional set and the seven caller\n  Queries keep their machines.\n- **Lint.** `make lint-model` gains `feature-entity-uniqueness`: under `Temporal.Feature` production\n  modules, an `entity` or `action` name declared twice is a violation unless allowlisted; the initial\n  allowlist records the duplicates that exist once the worker module lands (`workflow` in Caller,\n  Start, and Outage; `startWorkflow` in Start and Outage; `workerStop` in Caller, Outage, and Worker;\n  `workerResume` in Outage and Worker) each with the follow-up spec that removes it, test and\n  specimen modules are excluded, and the diagnostic names both modules. Any other duplicate fails. It reads `Registry.entities` in the environment-importing driver, since the\n  import-graph rules cannot see declarations.\n\n## API Contracts\n<!-- scope: technical -->\n\n- `compose` produces an `Umpire.Command.DeclaredModel`; `property`, `scenario`, `limits`, and\n  `query` accept it as they accept a machine, and a Query's `check` yields\n  `Umpire.Command.CheckedModel`. A `set` over a composed Model is rejected in version one with a\n  located error naming this spec's boundary; `case` needs no separate check because it realizes a\n  set.\n- A `verify` Query over a composed Model is searched by the backend `Selection.select` picks for\n  it. Its Limits are two-unit: on `veil`, `search` bounds product states and the depth is the\n  smaller of `steps` and `actions`; on `reference`, `search` bounds candidate paths. The Limits of\n  the two shipped Queries are declared so that both backends answer verified within limits, and the\n  differential line pins the backend, the reason, and both explored counts.\n- Every located error names the construct: unsynchronized shared action name, `sync:` participant\n  input domain mismatch, a `sync:` line naming a timer, a member field name containing `_`,\n  `restrict:` naming a timer or an absent action, `extend:` result at a disabled source or\n  duplicate, product above 16 results, reachable enumeration above the bound with its counts, a\n  failed `composedTableAgrees` check, a `set` over a composition, a `starts:` or `ends:` value that\n  names no member field.\n- A same-step Property may fix a state field; the refusals the predicate enumeration reports today\n  (`fixesNothing`, `notCarried` with the distinguishing step, `neverHolds`) are unchanged in shape.\n- Definition IDs of a composed Model hang off a `-compose-<name>` owner under the enclosing\n  namespace; member facts and outcomes keep their own IDs inside the union's constructors.\n\n## Quick commands\n\n```bash\ncd model && lake build Umpire.Command Temporal.Feature\ncd model && lake build UmpireTests TemporalModelTests   # every #guard_msgs pin, both differential sweeps\nmake umpire-gen-case-runtime-conformance && make umpire-check-case-runtime-conformance\nmake umpire-check-goldens && make canary-check-case\ngo test -tags test_dep ./tools/umpire/replay/... ./tools/umpire/evaluation/... ./tools/umpire/cmd/umpire-assess/... ./tools/umpire/authoring/... ./tools/umpire/vocabulary/...\nLEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 make lint-model\nmake umpire-check-regression   # final gate\n```\n\n## Edge Cases & Constraints\n<!-- scope: technical -->\n\n- **No fixture changes.** No entity, action, or machine moves in version one, and the Control rewrite\n  preserves its machine name, catalog keys, and result order, so every Case fixture, the canary\n  fixture, the canary policy's Case identity, the recorded control Run that three Go tests read, the\n  exploration coverage golden, and the replay bridge goldens are byte-identical. A byte change\n  anywhere is a finding, not a re-pin.\n- **Ordering with fn-89 and fn-90.** Both touched the pair fixture and `Pair/Tests.lean`; neither\n  touched `Pair/Model.lean`, the Control module, its fixture, or the recorded control Run. A pin taken against `cutover` false would move at the flip.\n- **Backend per Query.** No author mechanism forces a backend. A composed Property written with\n  `branches`, a guarded within-form, or a correlated rule, or a Limits unit of logical time,\n  search, or plans, falls back to `reference` with a receipt reason; the two shipped claims avoid\n  those forms so their differential lines read `veil default`. A future claim that needs one of\n  them still elaborates and is still compared by the differential.\n- **Predicate enumeration cost.** A same-step Property is enumerated over the composed table by\n  mutating each state field across the catalog; on `nexusCaller` that is about 316 reachable states\n  by 25 action classes. The seconds are recorded beside the kernel seconds and count against the\n  same elaboration budget.\n- **Bound pressure.** `nexusCaller` is at most 158 reachable operation states times 2 worker phases\n  over about 25 action classes, about 8k evaluations, under `enumerationBound`; the measured count\n  is a golden. A composition that exceeds the bound is refused with its counts; raising the bound is\n  a GOV-02 question only if a shipped composition needs it.\n- **Kernel cost.** The `composedTableAgrees` check and the law proof on a literal table of a few\n  hundred rows are measured on `workerOutage` first, which is the proof point. The decided `Bool`\n  compares constructor indices as `Nat`, which the kernel accelerates, and never sorts inside the\n  proof, because `List.mergeSort` is well-founded recursion the kernel cannot unfold; the kernel\n  honours `maxHeartbeats` and ignores `maxRecDepth`. An\n  unsynchronized member action stays independently executable, so the exclusion is a `restrict:`\n  on the worker member, `handlerWorker`, whose catalog is pinned to have no resume.\n- **Whole-state or field requirement.** The predicate enumeration fixes a whole state only when\n  the accepted steps share one; on a composed table the other member varies, so a claim on one\n  member's field is carried only by the field-addressed requirement task .7 adds. Realizing a composed Model is the next spec.\n- No move of the `operation` entity, the caller actions, or the caller machines out of\n  `Temporal.Feature.Nexus.Caller`. That move re-pins every `temporal.nexus.caller.*` ID, the seven\n  caller fixtures, the canary fixture, the canary policy's Case identity, and the exploration golden.\n- No shared `workflow` entity module. The user's observation on\n2026-09-26 that the models read as separate scenarios rather than one model is correct. Version one\nships the composition primitive and the one entity module that costs no Case re-pin, verifies the\nfirst two cross-entity claims, and names the canary-re-pinning move and the entity-key grammar as\nthe follow-up decision.\n\n### Implementation Tradeoffs\n<!-- scope: technical -->\n\n- **`compose`, not `system`.** `system` is the reserved party and a Lean identifier in the elaborator;\n  reusing it collides with both.\n- **Generated unions, author-written state.** Predicates need field names, so the author writes the\n  state structure; catalog keys collide across members (`accepted` twice), so the command generates\n  the Action, Outcome, and Fact unions with member-prefixed keys. This trades the earlier \"generate\n  nothing\" stance for the only type shape that typechecks `step.facts`.\n- **Declared synchronization, not name matching.** Two modules' `workerStop` actions have\n  different Definition IDs, so synchronization pairs actions explicitly; a shared name without a\n  `sync:` line is an error rather than a silent independent step.\n- **Classless participants.** The worker's `serve` synchronizes with the classed `handlerReply`\n  without importing the caller's `Reply` domain into the worker module.\n- **Reachable enumeration, literal table.** The full product exceeds the bound; a BFS at\n  elaboration emitted as a literal keeps the kernel proof over a value rather than a computation.\n- **verify only in version one.** Realizing a composed Model needs a multi-member `Realizable`, an\n  acting-member resolution in the Producer, and fn-89's per-entity Rules across entities. That is a\n  Producer spec of its own; shipping composition for claims first is the smallest useful step.\n- **Control over Pair, Pair unchanged, bytes unchanged.** `extend:` removes one copy of the reply\n  logic now while the recorded control Run keeps its bytes; Pair needs a field-projecting `restrict:`\n  to fit `instances: 2` under the bound, which is deferred.\n- **Per-composition kernel check.** A generic theorem about the composition function says nothing\n  about a given literal, so each composition carries its own decided check, the same shape the\n  refinement decision uses.\n- **Backend by selection, not by declaration.** fn-88 gave `Selection.select` the choice per\n  Query and no author key; this spec keeps it so and ships claims in the clause kinds that lower,\n  because a per-composition backend key would be a second selection rule the differential cannot\n  see.\n- **Member fields flattened, member structures kept.** The author's `state:` structure keeps one\n  field per member for predicates to read; the lowered state fields are the members' fields under\n  `<field>_` keys, because the clause language fixes one field at a time and refuses a disjunction\n  across fields.\n- **Underscore keys, dotted references.** `FiniteCatalog.validKey` admits no `.`, and `instances:`\n  already spells its product keys with `_`; a second separator would be a second grammar for the\n  same thing. Authors keep the dotted spelling and the elaborator resolves it.\n- **Field-addressed requirements as their own task.** The enumeration fixes whole states today, so\n  a nested-field claim on a composed table fixes nothing; the Outage claim can name its unique\n  state, the caller claim cannot, and the field requirement is the smallest addition that makes a\n  member's field a claim. It lands after the compose command and before the caller composition,\n  and its evaluators need no change.\n- **A restricted worker for the caller.** An unsynchronized member action is independently\n  executable, so \"no resume\" is a `restrict:` on the member and not a sentence.\n- Maintainability (plan review): duplication - none identified; structure - task .7's machine-side\n  test first imported `Temporal.Feature.Nexus.Caller.Model` into the Umpire test tree (round 2), a\n  back-edge `lint-model` forbids; replaced by a local synthetic multi-field machine.\n- **Refreshed 2026-09-27 against fn-88, fn-89, fn-90, and fn-94.** fn-88's seam, cutover, replay\n  gate, and registry-driven differential replaced the \"reference within Limits\" contingency; fn-89's\n  instanced Rules stay on the Case side, which no composition reaches; fn-90 left the Control\n  module and its Run untouched; fn-94 removed nothing this spec cites.\n- **Rules to draft under GOV-02**, new rules with the `*(drafted by fn-92; awaiting GOV-02\n  approval.)*` marker after the rule title and amendments as `*Amendment (drafted by fn-92; awaiting\n  GOV-02 approval.)*` continuation paragraphs, the two forms fn-88's drafts use: AUT-07a (add\n  `compose`, `restrict:`, `extend:` to the surface); glossary Machine (derived machines),\n  Refinement (a composition does not refine), Table (a composition's table holds reachable rows), a\n  new Composition entry, Party (distinguish the `compose` command from the `system` party); AUT-09\n  note that a reachable domain computed from declared member tables is author-provided; MOD-11\n  amendment and a new MOD-18 for `feature-entity-uniqueness`, with the `UMPIRE4_SPEC_MODEL_ARCH.md`\n  sentence that the import-graph phase is the single enforcement mechanism amended to name the\n  declaration-level rule.\n- **Rejected:** moving the caller module now (canary re-pin without a decision); a shared workflow\n  lifecycle for Start and Outage (different start evidence and different keys); running the caller\n  set over the composition (rewrites seven fixtures and the canary); name-based synchronization\n  (silent cross-module coupling); full-product enumeration (millions of evaluations); a\n  message-passing actor composition (second language).\n\n## Early proof point\n\nTask fn-92-compose-entity-machines-into-one-system.3 validates the core approach: it declares the\n`workerOutage` composition over the unchanged Outage machine and the new worker machine, its\nreachable table is under the bound, its `composedTableAgrees` check and law proof close in the\nkernel within budget, the stopped-worker claim verifies, and its Temporal differential line reads\n`veil default` with both backends agreeing. Multiple existing clauses cannot in general represent a compound antecedent: `(A and B) implies P` is not equivalent to requiring both `A implies P` and `B implies P`. This design therefore includes a small typed Boolean predicate vocabulary: atomic typed patterns, nonempty `all`/`any`, and `not`. Literal `one of` lowers to `any` over same-field equality atoms. The bounded universal Query establishes a terminal model response within one\\n    13\\t   semantic transition. This is finite model assurance, not an Observation, runtime delivery, or\\n    14\\t   wall-clock claim.\\n    15\\t3. `Authoring.lean` shows the default typed constructors for the baseline and guarded race.\\n    16\\t   `Tests.lean` checks semantic admission, equivalence, negative cases, coverage, and conflicts.\\n    17\\t   `AuthoringTests.lean` compares those constructors with the isolated `property%`, `behavior%`,\\n    18\\t   and `query%` specimens. Both test roots are imported by `TemporalModelTests`.\\n    19\\t4. `EVIDENCE.md` maps every prototype requirement to executable declarations and records the\\n    20\\t   exact residual differences from the deferred ordinary-authoring specification.\\n    21\\t\\n    22\\tThe authoring sequence is `FiniteTable.validate` / `checkModelTarget`, then `PropertySpec.check`,\\n    23\\t`ExactSequenceSpec.check`, and `QuerySpec.check`, followed by planning with\\n    24\\t`IncrementalPlannerKernel.ofCheckedQuery`. Raw declarations remain available for negative tests.\\n    25\\tA checked value exists only on the successful checker branch; the frontend alternatives do not\\n    26\\tcreate kernel-checked constants automatically.\\n    27\\t\\n    28\\t`Authoring.lean` keeps ordinary typed constructors as the default Nexus2 authoring surface. The\\n    29\\tcompiled `property%`, `behavior%`, and `query%` alternatives remain in `AuthoringTests.lean` for\\n    30\\tcomparison. All three lower to the existing Property, Behavior, and Query checkers; they add source\\n    31\\toccurrence capture and do not add an evaluator or migrate any production declaration.\\n    32\\t\\n    33\\tThe constructor and frontend specimens use the same explicit definition-family roots, kinds, keys,\\n    34\\tTarget, capabilities, Property clauses, named Behavior occurrences, Limits, and planner policy.\\n    35\\tCompilation checks all three baseline cases plus the cancellation race and guarded cases. The tests\\n    36\\tcompare every checked identity, canonical metadata value, behavior fingerprint, semantic field, and\\n    37\\tthe selected planner outcomes. They also compare the guarded Query's `found` result and all three\\n    38\\tbaseline planning outcomes. Moving a Behavior or Query declaration changes its checked source;\\n    39\\tBehavior's display-oriented canonical JSON changes as well, while semantic fingerprints remain\\n    40\\tequal. Query canonical metadata deliberately excludes source and remains equal.\\n    41\\t\\n    42\\t## Diagnostics and admission\\n    43\\t\\n    44\\tClosed frontend expressions run the existing checker during elaboration only to select a diagnostic.\\n    45\\tFailures freeze the complete typed error JSON, all related definition IDs, the selected source role,\\n    46\\tand the exact start/end compiler span. The matrix covers malformed and duplicate IDs, unknown Action,\\n    47\\tState, and result references, wrong reference kinds, missing capabilities and Properties, Target\\n    48\\tmismatch, resulting-state guards, unsupported roles/operators, empty Boolean/case/Query groups,\\n    49\\tinvalid and omitted units, and duplicate Query Properties. Parent, case, exception, clause, setup,\\n    50\\toccurrence, Action, Target, Property, Behavior, Limits, and policy roles are retained where relevant.\\n    51\\tThe omitted-unit case is a Lean structure-construction diagnostic because every raw `Limit` requires\\n    52\\tits unit; `QueryLimitSpec` avoids that omission by mapping its three named fields to fixed units.\\n    53\\t\\n    54\\tContradictory setup bindings are valid Behavior input with an explicit `unsatisfiable` space status;\\n    55\\tthe frontend test freezes that status instead of inventing an error. Contradictory reachable Property\\n    56\\tscenarios and missing exception replacements remain findings from the existing case analysis, with\\n    57\\ttheir realized state, Action, case, exception, and clause provenance. Resulting and future conditions\\n    58\\tin a trigger or exception remain rejected by the existing Property checker.\\n    59\\t\\n    60\\tFor terms containing local variables, compiler evaluation is skipped and the frontend returns the\\n    61\\tordinary typed checker expression. Invalid open-term Behavior and Query fixtures evaluate to their\\n    62\\ttyped error variants and cannot produce a partial checked value. The successful-branch Query form\\n    63\\taccepts `Option (QueryAuthoringInput LawStatement)`: outer `none` means prerequisite Target/Property/\\n    64\\tBehavior construction did not produce an input, while `some (.error error)` is the Query checker's\\n    65\\ttyped rejection. Closed diagnostic fixtures always use the latter path.\\n    66\\t\\n    67\\t## Conditions, exceptions, and bounded analysis\\n    68\\t\\n    69\\tThe portable Boolean vocabulary is limited to typed atoms over the declared prior state, selected\\n    70\\tAction, resulting state, Model Outcome, and Model Facts, composed with `all`, `any`, `not`, and\\n    71\\t`oneOf`. Guard inputs are checked before evaluation. Resulting-state and future-value conditions\\n    72\\tare rejected where trigger-time semantics cannot supply them; arbitrary comparisons, callbacks,\\n    73\\tand cross-field equality are unsupported.\\n    74\\t\\n    75\\tA conditional Property can pass because its trigger never occurred. That does not establish case\\n    76\\tcoverage. Complete case groups separately report whether the parent and every named case were\\n    77\\texercised. An exception narrows applicability at the original trigger; an exception without a\\n    78\\treplacement is reported and never invents behavior, and a condition first true on a later step\\n    79\\tcannot withdraw an already-triggered temporal obligation.\\n    80\\t\\n    81\\tAll applicable clauses and Properties are conjunctive. Source order, case order, and specificity\\n    82\\tdo not choose a winner. Mutually exclusive scalar expectations are a logical conflict; expectations\\n    83\\tthat are separately satisfiable but cannot coexist on any admitted Target continuation are modeled\\n    84\\tincompatibility. A single failed obligation is only a violation. Exhaustive absence applies solely\\n    85\\tto the enumerated finite space and declared Limits; `limit-reached` is inconclusive.\\n    86\\t\\n    87\\t## Admission trust experiment\\n    88\\t\\n    89\\t`PropertySpec.checked`, `ExactSequenceSpec.checked`, and `QuerySpec.checked` expose explicit-proof\\n    90\\tseams. The prototype attempted kernel success proofs through `rfl`, `decide`, and `decide +kernel`.\\n    91\\tProperty still fails for both the full baseline and a minimal closed declaration, including an\\n    92\\towner-local probe where private helpers were visible. The actual guarded Behavior and the explicit\\n    93\\tsuccessful-branch Query also fail `decide +kernel`; checked compiler fixtures retain those failures.\\n    94\\tNo attempt reported a heartbeat or recursion-depth limit, so the deeper reduction barrier remains\\n    95\\tunidentified.\\n    96\\t\\n    97\\tThe practical frontend therefore returns and recomputes the existing successful checker branch. It\\n    98\\tdoes not turn elaborator evaluation into a `CheckedProperty`, `CheckedBehavior`, or `CheckedQuery`\\n    99\\tconstant. The successful-branch Query input is assembled only from existing checked constructor\\n   100\\tresults. No new native extraction, `checkedTarget` default, `sorry`, `admit`, or custom axiom is used.\\n   101\\t`#print axioms` audits the constructor families, each check and explicit-proof seam, the guarded and\\n   102\\tbaseline frontend admissions, the measured Query frontend, and `Race.targetResult`. The prepared\\n+Contract implements the internal execution MonitorFactory; `New` creates a fresh `Evaluator`\\n+for every Run. The public Case facade binds that factory and does not accept replacement monitors.\\n+\\n+`Observe` processes an appended event synchronously. It stages rule transitions, scalar captures,\\n+and supporting sequence references, checks cancellation, then commits the entire event atomically.\\n+Predicates see pre-transition captures. Event-kind indexes preserve declaration order and only the\\n+first matching transition runs. The first committed violation returns `Stop`; later drain/cleanup\\n+events cannot extend or erase the proved bad prefix. Captures retain independent values and their\\n+producing event sequences. Rules and Runs never share mutable state.\\n+\\n+Pending liveness expires before transitions at the first recorded elapsed coordinate greater than\\n+or equal to its Run-relative horizon. A witness must be strictly earlier. Early completed closure\\n+is inconclusive. `RunEvent.execution_incomplete` takes effect before expiry and remains effective\\n+for later events, even when they omit the flag. Pending rules then stay inconclusive past their\\n+horizon; time and late witnesses cannot manufacture a result.\\n+\\n+The Executor records `Run.evaluation_failure_sequence` when an Observe callback fails after event\\n+append. It identifies the first callback whose staged evaluation did not commit. The evaluator\\n+freezes on that failure; later cleanup events may still be recorded. A successful Observe return\\n+is the commit boundary: the Executor must not reinterpret a later `ctx.Err()` as failure of that\\n+already committed event. Offline `Evaluate` replays\\n+only events before that coordinate through the same `Observe` implementation. A Close failure\\n+makes the final disposition incomplete without suppressing proofs already committed by Observe.\\n+No final disposition is retroactively applied to earlier events.\\n+\\n+Contract work counts indexed rule visits, expression operations/value bytes, projection traversal,\\n+and capture copies/references. Static preparation bounds that work per event and for the admitted\\n+Run event ceiling; runtime checks both ceilings and capture count/bytes before commit. Run input\\n+validation has separate bounded IR surface/type/fanout checks under Program response limits.\\n+The shared `internal/ir` interpreter only resolves values from its supplied typed environment;\\n+verification supplies declared Observations, captures, and the closed Run metadata fields.\\n+\\n+`Evaluate` and live `Close` produce independent protobuf Verdicts. The internal ordered transition\\n+trace and support sequences are deterministic and tested alongside deterministic Verdict bytes\\n+for completed, stopped, and incomplete Runs. --git a/tools/umpire/verification/README.md b/tools/umpire/verification/README.md\\nnew file mode 100644\\nindex 000000000..c6b73fe35\\n--- /dev/null\\n+++ b/tools/umpire/verification/README.md\\n@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@\\n+# Contract evaluation\\n+\\n+`Prepare` binds a Contract to the immutable Program Observation/bounds view. The prepared\\n+Contract implements the internal execution MonitorFactory; `New` creates a fresh `Evaluator`\\n+for every Run. The public Case facade binds that factory and does not accept replacement monitors.\\n+\\n+`Observe` processes an appended event synchronously. It stages rule transitions, scalar captures,\\n+and supporting sequence references, checks cancellation, then commits the entire event atomically.\\n+Predicates see pre-transition captures. Event-kind indexes preserve declaration order and only the\\n+first matching transition runs. The first committed violation returns `Stop`; later drain/cleanup\\n+events cannot extend or erase the proved bad prefix. Captures retain independent values and their\\n+producing event sequences. Rules and Runs never share mutable state.\\n+\\n+Pending liveness expires before transitions at the first recorded elapsed coordinate greater than\\n+or equal to its Run-relative horizon. A witness must be strictly earlier. Early completed closure\\n+is inconclusive. `RunEvent.execution_incomplete` takes effect before expiry and remains effective\\n+for later events, even when they omit the flag. Pending rules then stay inconclusive past their\\n+horizon; time and late witnesses cannot manufacture a result.\\n+\\n+The Executor records `Run.evaluation_failure_sequence` when an Observe callback fails after event\\n+append. It identifies the first callback whose staged evaluation did not commit. The evaluator\\n+freezes on that failure; later cleanup events may still be recorded. A successful Observe return\\n+is the commit boundary: the Executor must not reinterpret a later `ctx.Err()` as failure of that\\n+already committed event. Offline `Evaluate` replays\\n+only events before that coordinate through the same `Observe` implementation. A Close failure\\n+makes the final disposition incomplete without suppressing proofs already committed by Observe.\\n+No final disposition is retroactively applied to earlier events.\\n+\\n+Contract work counts indexed rule visits, expression operations/value bytes, projection traversal,\\n+and capture copies/references. Supporting designs cite rules by ID. MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY indicate\\n requirement strength.\\n \\n ## Governance\\n \\n - **GOV-01 — Stable rule IDs.** New rules MUST receive new IDs. Existing IDs MUST NOT be renumbered\\n   or reused, even after a rule is retired.\\n - **GOV-02 — Human approval.** A human MUST approve any deliberate exception to these rules.\\n \\n The term definitions in this document are normative. Supporting documents MUST use those terms\\n consistently. Capitalized terms have Umpire-specific meanings. Exact Lean names appear in backticks.\\n \\n ## How Umpire works\\n \\n Umpire models expected behavior. A Query asks a bounded question about that behavior, and planning\\n searches for an answer. When planning selects a Model Trace, it packages an Execution Plan for the\\n trace with its Properties and Limits as a Test Plan. Execution attempts the Test Plan against\\n Temporal. Run Evaluation uses the resulting Evidence to check the selected trace and its\\n Properties. For example, a Nexus Property can require that closing a Workflow cancels its running\\n Nexus operation at most once.\\n \\n ## How the model is organized\\n \\n ### Core concepts\\n \\n - **Behavior Model.** Lean code under `model/` that describes expected product behavior and\\n   Temporal's current implementation behavior.\\n - **Model Definition.** A named, handwritten part of the Behavior Model, such as a state, Action,\\n   transition, or Property. Generated Data and Generated Views are not Model Definitions.\\n - **Generated Data.** Machine-produced descriptions of API and configuration fields and types. This\\n   data describes what information exists, not how it affects behavior.\\n - **Definition ID.** A stable dot-separated ID for a Model Definition, such as\\n   `workflow-nexus.property.caller-closure`. Umpire checks that an ID refers to the expected kind of\\n   definition. Reordering declarations or editing documentation does not change it.\\n - **Behavior Fingerprint.** A value computed from the behavior-affecting parts of a Model Definition.\\n   It changes with behavior, but not with documentation, source location, or source order.\\n - **Capability Contract.** A named behavior that one model component requires and another provides,\\n   together with the laws each provider must satisfy.\\n - **Implementation Link.** Lean code that explicitly connects product behavior in\\n   `Temporal.Feature` to corresponding implementation behavior in `Temporal.System` without merging\\n   their descriptions.\\n \\n ### Where things live\\n \\n - **`Umpire`.** Reusable Lean tools for authoring and checking models and producing plans. It\\n   contains no Temporal-specific behavior.\\n - **`Temporal.Feature`.** Product behavior visible to users and SDKs, independent of the current\\n   implementation.\\n - **`Temporal.System`.** Behavior of the current Temporal implementation, configuration, and\\n   runtime.\\n - **`Temporal.API`.** Generated API field and type information from Protobuf and gRPC definitions.\\n - **`Temporal.DynamicConfig`.** Generated configuration field and type information.\\n \\n ### Purpose and scope\\n \\n - **SCP-01 — Temporal-driven scope.** Umpire MUST include only capabilities required by a concrete\\n   Temporal use case in modeling, Regression, Exploration, Run Evaluation, or verification.\\n - **SCP-02 — Reusable core.** Reusable `Umpire` code MUST NOT contain Temporal-specific names,\\n   dependencies, or fixtures.\\n - **SCP-03 — Lean Behavior Model.** All Behavior Model code MUST be written in Lean and live under\\n   `model/`.\\n - **SCP-04 — Complement specialized tests.** Umpire SHOULD complement specialized unit, race,\\n   persistence, schema, authorization, performance, and handler tests rather than replace them.\\n \\n ### Source of truth\\n \\n - **SEM-01 — Model authority.** For behavior covered by Umpire, the Behavior Model MUST be the only\\n   source of truth. Generated code, Artifacts, runtimes, Evidence mappings, and checker adapters MUST\\n   NOT add or override behavior.\\n - **SEM-02 — Model Definitions.** Handwritten `Temporal.Feature` and `Temporal.System` Model\\n   Definitions MUST be the only sources of product and implementation behavior.\\n - **SEM-03 — Generated Data.** Generated `Temporal.API` and `Temporal.DynamicConfig` declarations\\n   MUST NOT define behavior until a Model Definition interprets them.\\n - **SEM-08 — Explicit Implementation Link.** A dedicated Implementation Link MUST connect\\n   `Temporal.Feature` product behavior to `Temporal.System` implementation behavior. Declaration\\n   order and implicit selection MUST NOT create that connection.\\n+- **SEM-10 — Portable interpreter seam.** Lean MUST compile a selected checked Test into its\\n+  Portable Evaluation Contract. The contract and its fixed-version interpreter MUST NOT add,\\n+  select, override, or retrieve behavior independently of that checked model input.\\n \\n ### Enforced module boundaries\\n \\n - **MOD-01 — `Umpire` independence.** `Umpire.*` MUST NOT directly or transitively import\\n   `Temporal.*`.\\n - **MOD-03 — `Temporal.Feature` isolation.** `Temporal.Feature.*` MUST NOT directly or transitively\\n   import `Temporal.System.*`. Imports of `Temporal.Verify.*` or `Umpire.Verify.Veil` are allowed only\\n   for the verification consumers listed in MOD-05.\\n - **MOD-05 — Verification isolation.** First-party (repository-owned) Lean modules MUST NOT directly\\n   or transitively import `Temporal.Verify.*` or `Umpire.Verify.Veil` unless they are one of these\\n   opt-in consumers: `TemporalVerify`, `TemporalVeilTests`, `Temporal.Tool.VerifyVeil`, or\\n   `Temporal.Feature.Nexus.Experimental.CallerClosure.VeilTests`.\\n - **MOD-09 — `Shared` independence.** `Shared.*` MUST NOT directly or transitively import `Umpire.*`\\n   or `Temporal.*`.\\n - **MOD-10 — `Temporal.System` isolation.** `Temporal.System.*` MUST NOT directly or transitively\\n   import `Temporal.Feature.*`. The only exception is `Temporal.System.Nexus.ImplementationLink`.\\n - **MOD-11 — Executable enforcement.** `make lint-model` MUST enforce MOD-01, MOD-03, MOD-05,\\n   MOD-09, and MOD-10 across the complete first-party Lean import graph.\\n \\n ### Module design\\n \\n - **MOD-02 — Product and system ownership.** `Temporal.Feature` MUST own product-visible behavior.\\n   `Temporal.System` MUST own implementation mechanisms, configuration interpretation, Evidence\\n   mappings, and Execution behavior.\\n - **MOD-04 — Independent product and system modules.** `Temporal.Feature.*` and\\n   `Temporal.System.*` modules MUST be understandable and testable on their own. Only focused\\n   Implementation Link modules MAY connect them, subject to MOD-10.\\n - **MOD-06 — Small public interfaces.** `Umpire.*` modules SHOULD hide checking, planning, Artifact,\\n   observation, and verification machinery behind small, cohesive interfaces.\\n - **MOD-07 — Clear component boundaries.** Components MUST have narrow responsibilities and\\n   communicate through explicit contracts rather than each other's internal representations.\\n - **MOD-08 — Isolated testability.** Each component MUST be testable with fixtures or generic\\n   examples without the complete `Umpire` pipeline or a running Temporal cluster.\\n \\n ## Model authoring and traces\\n \\n ### Trace concepts\\n \\n - **Action.** Something a Test asks the model to do, such as closing a Workflow. An Action request\\n   neither chooses its Model Outcome nor proves that the Action occurred at runtime.\\n - **Model Outcome.** The next state and Model Facts that the Target produces for an Action. It is an\\n   expected model result, not a runtime result or Stage Status.\\n - **Model Fact.** A claim made by the model, such as “the Nexus operation received a cancellation.”\\n   Logs, spans, RPCs, and records are Evidence used to determine whether the claim was true during a\\n   Run.\\n - **Model Trace.** A starting state and a sequence of Actions, Model Outcomes, state changes, and\\n   Model Facts. It contains no runtime Evidence.\\n - **Scenario.** A named set of possible Model Traces. It defines available variations and faults but\\n   does not select a trace.\\n - **Known Gap.** A missing or unsupported Capability Contract, input, interpretation, or claim. A\\n   Known Gap limits what an Artifact or Result can prove.\\n - **Behavior (`Umpire.Behavior`).** Lean data that defines the Model Traces a Scenario allows. It\\n   neither evaluates Properties nor determines whether a trace occurred at runtime.\\n - **Target (`Umpire.CheckedTarget`).** A validated Behavior Model shared by Properties, Behaviors,\\n   and Queries. It is ready for planning and evaluation.\\n - **Property (`Umpire.Property`).** A reusable pass/fail rule over Model Traces. For example, closing\\n   a Workflow cancels its running Nexus operation at most once.\\n - **Query (`Umpire.Query`).** A request, within explicit Limits, to verify a Property, find a\\n   satisfying witness or violating counterexample, or select a Model Trace for Exploration.\\n - **Unsatisfiable.** A Behavior that allows no Model Traces. This is an error, not a passing Test.\\n \\n ### Model languages\\n \\n - **SEM-04 — Separate languages.** Each Lean authoring language—including `Umpire.Property`,\\n   `Umpire.Behavior`, `Umpire.Query`, and `Umpire.Observation`—MUST be separate and have a distinct\\n   purpose.\\n - **SEM-05 — Pure `Umpire.Property`.** `Umpire.Property` declarations MUST use only Model Traces and\\n   Capability Contracts. They MUST NOT depend on implementation Evidence.\\n - **SEM-06 — Declarative `Umpire.Behavior`.** `Umpire.Behavior` declarations MUST constrain\\n   allowed Model Traces. They MUST NOT become step-by-step RPC or runtime scripts.\\n - **SEM-07 — Model-owned outcomes.** Authors MUST request Actions, while `Umpire.CheckedTarget`\\n   determines their Model Outcomes and resulting states.\\n - **SEM-09 — Bounded progress.** A Property claiming that something eventually happens MUST state a\\n   Limit and unit. A finite Execution MUST NOT prove an unlimited “eventually” claim.\\n \\n ### Authoring\\n \\n - **AUT-01 — Approachable authoring.** A Temporal engineer with basic Lean knowledge SHOULD be able\\n   to write ordinary Model Definitions without understanding Umpire's implementation details.\\n - **AUT-02 — Explicit meaning.** Authoring interfaces MUST make states, Actions, Model Outcomes,\\n   relations, Limits, faults, Capability Contracts, Known Gaps, and unsupported cases explicit.\\n - **AUT-03 — Checked declarations.** Public declarations MUST be checked before planning or\\n   Execution. Failures SHOULD report errors at the relevant source location.\\n - **AUT-04 — Stable IDs.** Every public Model Definition MUST have a stable, dot-separated Definition\\n   ID that is checked against the expected definition kind. Source order and documentation MUST NOT\\n   affect it.\\n - **AUT-05 — Portable data.** Anything used in portable planning, Artifacts, promotion, or\\n   cross-language Execution MUST be serializable data that Lean can interpret. It MUST NOT depend on\\n   in-process callbacks.\\n - **AUT-06 — Explicit composition.** Competing providers MUST be selected explicitly, and\\n   cross-domain relationships MUST be connected explicitly. Declaration order and Lean's automatic\\n   instance search MUST NOT choose behavior.\\n - **AUT-07 — Single authoring path.** `Umpire.Property`, `Umpire.Behavior`, and `Umpire.Query` MUST\\n   be the only public languages for declaring Properties, Scenarios, and Queries.\\n   `Umpire.CheckedTarget` is their shared model representation, not an authoring language. Wrappers\\n   MUST NOT provide another way to define behavior.\\n - **AUT-08 — Finite Target adapter.** Authors SHOULD use the proof-carrying\\n   `Umpire.FiniteMachine` adapter when a complete finite Target has enumerators that define its\\n   authoritative behavior. The adapter derives membership relations, completeness support, and\\n   exact finite planning. Authors MUST still provide ordered semantic domains, encoders, enumerators,\\n   evidence that enumerated values stay within those domains, and evidence that every enumerated\\n   Action is executable. As an expert alternative, authors MAY construct `Umpire.TransitionKernel`\\n   directly for Targets whose authority is specified independently. Both paths MUST produce an\\n   `Umpire.AuthoredTarget` and pass it to `Umpire.checkTarget`. `Umpire.FiniteMachine` MUST NOT\\n   introduce another Behavior, Property, Query, Scenario, or macro language.\\n \\n ## Planning, Limits, and Artifacts\\n \\n ### Planning and Artifact concepts\\n \\n - **Limit.** A typed limit for one stage, such as 100 search candidates or 30 execution steps. It\\n   does not limit any other stage.\\n - **Limit Reached.** A Stage Status reported when a stage reaches a Limit before answering its\\n   question. It proves neither a negative answer nor that the search was exhaustive.\\n - **Exhaustive Search.** A search that checks every candidate allowed by the exact Behavior and\\n   Limits. If it finds no candidate, it proves absence only within those Limits.\\n - **Test.** A deterministic Model Trace selected from a Scenario and packaged with its Properties\\n   and Limits as a Test Plan.\\n - **Artifact.** Immutable, versioned, inspectable data exchanged across components, languages, and\\n   processes. Artifacts cannot define model behavior.\\n+- **Portable Evaluation Contract.** A versioned, closed, per-Test Artifact that Lean derives from\\n+  one selected checked Test, its Observation, Implementation Link, Properties, Limits, Known Gaps,\\n+  Definition IDs, and Behavior Fingerprints for interpretation without a Lean runtime. It is\\n+  portable model-derived data, not another authoring language or behavioral authority.\\n - **Artifact Checksum.** A reproducible checksum over all Artifact content in canonical order,\\n   excluding the checksum field itself. It identifies one exact Artifact; it is not a Definition ID\\n   or Behavior Fingerprint.\\n - **Generated View.** A deterministic representation of an Artifact, such as a Go test or\\n   documentation. It is bound to the source Artifact Checksum and cannot define behavior.\\n - **Execution Plan (`Umpire.DrivePlan`).** Generated instructions for attempting a selected Model\\n   Trace. It is not Evidence that Execution occurred.\\n - **Test Plan (`Umpire.ExperimentSpec`).** A portable Artifact containing an Execution Plan and all\\n   other data needed to attempt one bounded Test. It describes the intended Test, not what happened.\\n \\n ### Planning and Limit rules\\n \\n - **PLN-01 — Explicit Limits.** Separate, explicit, typed Limits MUST govern each stage: checking\\n   whether a Behavior allows a Model Trace, search, Execution, Observation Evaluation, and failure\\n   reduction.\\n - **PLN-02 — Deterministic selection.** Identical Model Definitions, model inputs, Limits, strategy,\\n   and seed MUST produce identical Execution Plans and Artifact Checksums.\\n - **PLN-03 — Exhaustive means complete.** A search declared Exhaustive MUST fail if it cannot check\\n   every candidate.\\n - **PLN-04 — Limit Reached is inconclusive.** Limit Reached MUST NOT be treated as proof that no\\n   trace or counterexample exists.\\n - **PLN-05 — Unsatisfiable is an error.** A checked `Umpire.Behavior` that admits no Model Trace MUST\\n   report `unsatisfiable`, never a passing Test.\\n - **PLN-06 — Generated Execution Plan.** A `Umpire.DrivePlan` MUST contain generated instructions.\\n   It MUST NOT be an authoring language or Evidence that Execution occurred.\\n \\n ### Artifact rules\\n \\n - **ART-01 — Versioned formats.** Persisted Artifacts MUST use versioned, inspectable formats and\\n   deterministic serialization.\\n - **ART-02 — Model binding.** Artifacts MUST carry Definition IDs, Behavior Fingerprints, their own\\n   Artifact Checksums, source information, Known Gaps, and enough compatibility data for stale readers\\n   to reject them.\\n - **ART-03 — Portable Test Plan.** `Umpire.ExperimentSpec` MUST contain complete,\\n   environment-independent instructions for one bounded Test. It MUST NOT claim that any requested\\n   Action, fault, Model Outcome, or observation occurred.\\n - **ART-04 — Safe format changes.** Readers MUST reject unknown major versions and unknown fields\\n   that could affect behavior. Changing the meaning of old data requires a named, deterministic\\n   migration.\\n - **ART-05 — Same experiment.** Local, CI, staging, black-box, and canary Execution MUST all use the\\n   same Test Plan. Environment-specific copies MUST NOT change modeled behavior.\\n - **ART-06 — Complete traces.** An executable trace MUST include its model setup, participant\\n   programs, references whose concrete IDs are resolved at runtime, Actions, faults, ordering,\\n   observations, termination, and cleanup obligations.\\n - **ART-07 — Generated Views.** The same source Artifact MUST always produce the same Generated View.\\n   Generated Go tests and documentation MUST be bound to their source Artifact Checksums and MUST NOT\\n   be editable sources of model behavior.\\n+- **ART-08 — Closed portable evaluation.** A Portable Evaluation Contract MUST use a versioned,\\n+  finite operator vocabulary, be closed over one exact Test, carry its source bindings and Limits,\\n+  and contain no callback, executable, environment selector, registry lookup, or extension hook.\\n+  Admission MUST reject unknown major versions, fields, enum values, operators, crossed bindings,\\n+  and noncanonical bytes before runtime I/O.\\n \\n ## Execution, Evidence, and Run Evaluation\\n \\n ### Execution and Evidence concepts\\n \\n - **Execution.** A bounded attempt to run a Test Plan in an environment. It records what happened\\n   but does not decide whether a Property passed.\\n - **Run.** The record of one Execution in one environment, including attempts to perform Actions and\\n   apply faults, receipts, Evidence, failures, and cleanup.\\n - **Fault Request.** A request to apply a fault at a specific point in a Model Trace. It does not\\n   prove that the fault occurred.\\n - **Execution Receipt.** Runtime Evidence confirming that a requested Action or fault occurred. It\\n   is tied to that request; planning or sending the request is not an Execution Receipt.\\n - **Evidence.** Logs, traces, responses, records, and receipts collected during a Run. Umpire checks\\n   their source, identity, order, and completeness before using them to establish Model Facts.\\n - **Evidence Link.** An auditable record of why Umpire accepted a Model Fact, including its mapping,\\n   Evidence records, bindings, ordering facts, and completeness checks.\\n - **Observation (`Umpire.Observation`).** The Lean authoring language for rules that translate raw\\n   Evidence into Model Facts while retaining source, order, completeness, conflict information, and\\n   Evidence Links.\\n - **Observation Evaluation.** The stage that applies an Observation to raw Evidence and produces\\n   Model Facts and Evidence Links.\\n - **Run Evaluation.** The process that uses Observation Evaluation to construct a Model Trace,\\n   translates the trace through any required Implementation Link, and evaluates its Properties. It\\n   decides what a Run proves but does not perform Execution.\\n - **Stage Status.** The status of one stage, such as planning, Execution, Observation Evaluation,\\n   Property checking, or verification. It says nothing about another stage unless a rule explicitly\\n   connects them.\\n - **Result.** The complete interpreted report for a Run. It keeps operational, Observation\\n   Evaluation, Implementation Link, Property, and cleanup statuses separate and records Known Gaps\\n   independently.\\n+- **Local Canary Decision.** A `pass`, `fail`, or `inconclusive` decision about only the exact Test\\n+  and Evidence named by one Portable Evaluation Contract. It is neither a Claim Assessment nor a\\n+  statement about model consistency, exhaustive coverage, compiler correctness, release\\n+  eligibility, or any other Test.\\n \\n ### Execution and Evidence rules\\n \\n - **EVD-01 — Thin runtime.** Runtime and CLI code MUST do no more than fill in environment-specific\\n   values and execute model-produced Artifacts. It MUST NOT independently decide Temporal product\\n   behavior.\\n - **EVD-02 — Separate Run Evaluation.** Execution MUST report what happened. Observation Evaluation,\\n   Implementation Link application, and Property evaluation MUST be separate steps that determine\\n   what the Evidence proves.\\n - **EVD-03 — Checked Evidence.** Before a Property uses raw Evidence, Umpire MUST normalize it;\\n   validate its source and identity; order it causally; check for missing records; and translate it\\n   into Model Facts.\\n - **EVD-04 — Fail closed.** Missing, ambiguous, conflicting, outdated, unsupported, or causally\\n   unrelated Evidence MUST NOT establish success or absence.\\n - **EVD-05 — Independent statuses.** Authoring, planning, Execution, Observation Evaluation,\\n   Implementation Link application, Property evaluation, and verification MUST report separate Stage\\n   Status values. A status for one stage MUST NOT imply the status of another.\\n - **EVD-06 — Execution Receipts.** A requested Action or fault MUST NOT count as having occurred\\n   without an Execution Receipt linked to the intended point in the Model Trace.\\n - **EVD-07 — Distributed ordering.** Conclusions about model behavior MUST rely only on\\n   model-declared order, causal relationships, or record order within one source. They MUST NOT rely\\n   on synchronized wall clocks.\\n - **EVD-08 — Complete lifecycle.** Every Run MUST retain Action and fault attempts, actual outcomes,\\n   Evidence, Known Gaps, divergence, infrastructure failures, and cleanup results.\\n - **EVD-09 — Evidence Links.** Every accepted Model Fact MUST retain an Evidence Link to its mapping,\\n   Evidence records, bindings, ordering facts, and completeness checks.\\n+- **EVD-10 — Strict portable interpretation.** A portable interpreter MUST evaluate only its\\n+  admitted contract's versioned operators, in canonical order, under precharged work and structural\\n+  Limits. Unknown, missing, conflicting, noncanonical, out-of-range, or unsupported semantics MUST\\n+  NOT produce a Local Canary Decision of `pass`.\\n \\n ## Exploration, replay, and promotion\\n \\n ### Exploration concepts\\n \\n - **Exploration.** Model-owned selection from a declared space to find useful Tests or\\n   counterexamples. It is exhaustive only when it covers the declared finite space within its\\n   Limits.\\n - **Regression.** A permanent named `Umpire.Query` retained to detect recurrence of known behavior\\n   independently of Exploration Limits.\\n - **Exact Replay.** Re-evaluation of a Model Trace or counterexample against the Behavior Model,\\n   using exactly the referenced Definition IDs, Behavior Fingerprints, Properties, Behavior, and\\n   Limits.\\n \\n ### Exploration rules\\n \\n - **EXP-01 — Shared model.** Regression Execution, model checking, Exploration, fuzzing, Exact\\n   Replay, and canary selection MUST reuse the same Model Definitions and\\n   `Umpire.Property` declarations.\\n - **EXP-02 — Model-owned Exploration.** The model MUST define the exploration space, allowed input\\n   variations, coverage criteria, candidate scoring, and selection rules. Orchestration MAY execute\\n   and store the resulting batches.\\n - **EXP-03 — Bounded fuzzing is not exhaustive.** Runtime fuzzing stopped by a time or work Limit\\n   MUST NOT claim exhaustive coverage.\\n - **EXP-04 — Pinned Regressions.** Known Regressions MUST run independently of Exploration Limits.\\n - **EXP-05 — Reviewed promotion.** Before human review for promotion to a permanent Lean Regression,\\n   a discovered failure MUST be reproduced at runtime, minimized in model terms, and validated by\\n   Exact Replay.\\n \\n ## Verification, CLI, and claims\\n \\n ### Verification and claim concepts\\n \\n - **`Temporal.Verify`.** Optional Temporal-specific checker integration. It does not define behavior.\\n - **`Umpire.Verify.Veil`.** Optional reusable Veil checker integration. Ordinary models and runtimes\\n   do not import it.\\n - **Assurance Method.** The basis for a claim, such as a kernel proof, reconstructed proof, trusted\\n   solver, search within Limits, Test execution, or concrete replay. These methods are not\\n   interchangeable.\\n - **Claim Assessment.** A statement of what a Result proves in a named environment under a specific\\n   Evidence policy. It includes the Limits, Assurance Method, Known Gaps, trusted sources, and cleanup\\n   status.\\n \\n ### Optional verification rules\\n \\n - **VER-01 — Lean-native default.** Lean-native checking MUST be the default verification path.\\n - **VER-02 — Explicit opt-in.** Each model family and each `Umpire.Property` declaration MUST opt in\\n   explicitly to optional checker integration.\\n - **VER-03 — Checked link.** Every representation used by an optional checker MUST have an explicit,\\n   checked link to an `Umpire.CheckedTarget` and an `Umpire.Property` declaration.\\n - **VER-04 — Complete verification receipts.** Verification receipts MUST expose source\\n   information, Definition IDs, Behavior Fingerprints, assumptions, Limits, Known Gaps, and an\\n   Assurance Method.\\n - **VER-05 — Exact Replay.** A checker counterexample MUST be validated by Exact Replay against the\\n   Behavior Model before it can support a claimed model violation or promotion to a Regression.\\n - **VER-06 — Distinct trust.** Kernel proofs, reconstructed proofs, trusted solvers, search within\\n   Limits, Test executions, and concrete replay MUST be distinct Assurance Methods.\\n \\n ### CLI, environment, and claim rules\\n \\n - **CLI-01 — Code location.** Umpire CLI code MUST either live under `tools/umpire` or be imported\\n   from `temporal/tools/common`.\\n - **CLI-02 — Thin interface.** User-facing tools MAY select declarations and tighten declared\\n   Limits. They MUST NOT invent `Umpire.Behavior` declarations or broaden model-declared Limits.\\n - **CLI-03 — Inspectability.** User-facing tools SHOULD provide consistent commands to list and\\n   explain named Properties, Scenarios, Tests, Explorations, verification checks, Artifacts, and\\n   Results.\\n - **QLF-01 — Environment settings.** Environment profiles MAY provide endpoints, credentials,\\n   namespaces, permissions, resources, and adapters, provided they do not change modeled behavior.\\n - **QLF-02 — Environment controls.** Each non-local environment MUST explicitly own its authorization\\n   controls, rate and concurrency limits, cleanup and isolation responsibilities, rollout policy,\\n   and limits on possible impact.\\n - **QLF-03 — Complete claims.** Every Claim No coercion. |\\n| Pattern | `natural_at_most` | canonical natural and bound → boolean | Match the exact Definition ID/field, then compare unsigned naturals. Noncanonical or out-of-range values are `unsupported`, not a Property violation. |\\n\\nEvery expression visit, rule/record candidate, emitted coordinate, link entry, clause/step pair, and\\npattern/value candidate costs one evaluation work unit in addition to the separately bounded input\\nrecords and bytes. Work is charged before evaluation; exact N is admitted and N+1 returns the\\nresponsible Limit status. Expression depth and collection cardinalities also have explicit Limits.\\nThe interpreter never relies on map iteration order: protobuf order is canonical and diagnostics use\\nthe first failing item in that order. Task `.5` proves Lean/Go parity for every row, success/failure\\nbranch, type mismatch, empty/missing input, and exact N/N+1 boundary, not merely the two final canned\\nverdicts.\\n\\n### Deep executor module\\n\\nThe external seam is one transport-independent interface conceptually equivalent to:\\n\\n```go\\nExecute(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)\\n```\\n\\n`Request` supplies admitted contract bytes and one exact admitted input set. The executor fills a\\nfresh opaque run identity only after single-flight admission succeeds. `Result` contains the complete\\nexecution/evaluation record and local decision. Contract admission,\\nrunner invocation, Evidence closure, portable evaluation, cleanup checking, and decision mapping\\nstay inside the module. HTTP is a thin adapter over this seam. The disposable-cluster and existing\\nloopback authorities are adapters below the same executor; callers do not orchestrate its phases.\\n\\nThe resident process may handle multiple bounded requests without restarting. Fn-28 does not add a\\nfleet scheduler, lease service, crash recovery, persistent queue, production deployment, or release\\ncontroller. Those can later reuse the executor interface without changing contract semantics.\\n\\n## API Contracts\\n<!-- scope: technical -->\\n\\n- Lean lowers a checked, selected Test into a complete per-test value. A Go packer may validate and\\n  deterministically encode that value, but it performs no semantic selection or lowering.\\n- Canonical contract bytes use deterministic protobuf serialization. Admission rejects unknown\\n  fields and enum values, unsupported major versions/operators, noncanonical bytes, invalid Limits,\\n  checksum mismatch, duplicate identities, and crossed Definition-ID/fingerprint bindings.\\n- The Go evaluator interprets only the bundled Observation mapping, trace projection,\\n  Implementation Link, and Property clauses. It never consults a model registry or synthesizes a\\n  missing clause.\\n- Evidence absence may establish a fact only after every contract-required source has explicitly\\n  closed. Wall-clock quiet periods never establish absence.\\n- Eventual Evidence collection uses contract-bounded source closure, cursor/watermark or terminal\\n  receipts, and a deadline. Reaching the deadline without closure returns an incomplete operational\\n  stage and `inconclusive`; it never returns `pass`.\\n- The detailed semantic statuses remain `satisfied`, `violated`, `unknown`, `conflict`, or\\n  `unsupported`. Canary mapping returns `pass` only for a fully closed successful run with accepted\\n  Observation Evaluation, applied Implementation Link, satisfied Property, and complete cleanup;\\n  returns `fail` only for a trustworthy closed `violated` verdict; and returns `inconclusive` for\\n  all operational, closure, unknown, conflict, unsupported, or tooling failures.\\n- The HTTP adapter accepts bounded protobuf request bytes and returns bounded protobuf result bytes.\\n  It exposes no arbitrary executable, checker path, Lean command, model selector, endpoint,\\n  credential, retry, or semantic override.\\n- One executor is single-flight. Its atomic state is `idle`, `active`, or `poisoned`. An overlapping\\n  request observes `active` and returns a typed `busy` tooling result plus local `inconclusive`\\n  before runtime I/O. State returns to `idle` only after complete cleanup; uncertain cleanup moves\\n  permanently to `poisoned`, whose requests also fail before runtime I/O. HTTP concurrency cannot\\n  bypass this admission.\\n- `testcore.NewEnv` owns the disposable cluster and SDK client. The Umpire adapter owns and cleans up\\n  only per-run workers, endpoints, workflows, correlations, and other run-created resources; it\\n  never closes or mutates the enclosing test harness outside the run contract.\\n\\n## Edge Cases & Constraints\\n<!-- scope: technical -->\\n\\n- Dynamic run IDs, workflow IDs, task queues, timestamps, and transport record IDs are normalized\\n  through contract-declared slots and correlations; expected output is stable semantic data, not a\\n  canned byte-for-byte runtime trace.\\n- Canned normal and negative-control contract protobufs are generated before the tagged test. The\\n  test process has no Lean dependency and does not shell out to Make, `mise`, `lake`, or `go test`.\\n- Duplicate, missing, ambiguous, causally unrelated, stale, unsupported, or post-closure Evidence\\n  fails closed according to the existing independent status model.\\n- One resident executor and one `testcore.NewEnv` cluster run both live contracts sequentially with\\n  fresh run isolation, proving process/cluster reuse. A poisoned or uncertain cleanup state prevents\\n  another request from being accepted by that executor instance.\\n- Overlapping HTTP requests are never queued or run concurrently. The loser receives the typed\\n  pre-I/O `busy`/`inconclusive` result; cancellation and cleanup of the active request complete\\n  before another request can observe `idle`.\\n- Cancellation closes every owned resource and returns an honest incomplete result. The executor\\n  never silently redispatches a possibly-started Test.\\n- Work and memory are limited independently for contract bytes, operators, Evidence records,\\n  Evidence collection, evaluation, HTTP bodies, and total request duration. N is admitted and N+1\\n  fails at the responsible seam.\\n- Existing comments in changed source remain intact.\\n\\n## Quick commands\\n\\n```bash\\nmake proto\\ncd model && mise exec -- lake build Temporal.Tool.PortableEvaluationContractTests\\ngo test -count=1 -tags test_dep ./tools/umpire/evaluationcontract/... ./tools/umpire/portableevaluation/... ./tools/umpire/executor/...\\ngo test -count=1 -tags 'test_dep integration' ./tests -run '^TestUmpirePortableCanaryExecutor$'\\nmake lint-model\\nmake umpire-check-regression\\nmake lint-code\\n```\\n\\n## Acceptance Criteria\\n<!-- scope: both -->\\n\\n- **R1:** A versioned protobuf `EvaluationContract`, the exact version-one operator table above, and\\n  result vocabulary live under the conventional\\n  internal Umpire proto package, generate normal Go bindings, serialize deterministically, and fail\\n  closed on unknown or noncanonical input.\\n- **R2:** Lean is the only semantic compiler. It lowers the exact selected Test, Observation,\\n  Implementation Link, Property clauses, Limits, Known Gaps, Definition IDs, and Behavior\\n  Fingerprints into a closed per-test contract; Go performs only structural packing and execution.\\n- **R3:** A generic Go interpreter with no Lean dependency reconstructs the Evidence-backed trace,\\n  applies the bundled link, evaluates the bundled clauses, and produces the existing independent\\n  detailed statuses plus a correct local canary decision.\\n- **R4:** Evidence collection supports eventual consistency only through explicit bounded closure.\\n  Complete positive and negative Evidence decides; deadline, ambiguity, conflict, unsupported data,\\n  missing closure, or uncertain cleanup is inconclusive and never success.\\n- **R5:** One deep resident executor module hides atomic single-flight admission, execution, Evidence\\n  closure, evaluation, and cleanup behind one small interface; a thin bounded HTTP adapter can serve\\n  multiple sequential requests without starting a new Go or Lean process and rejects overlap before\\n  runtime I/O.\\n- **R6:** One tagged Go integration test using `testcore.NewEnv` keeps one disposable cluster and one\\n  executor process alive, runs the pre-generated normal and duplicate-delivery contracts with fresh\\n  isolation, and observes respectively a local pass and a trustworthy local fail without invoking\\n  Lean.\\n- **R7:** The contract and result explicitly limit the local verdict to one exact Test. Whole-model\\n  validity, exhaustive coverage, compiler correctness, release eligibility, and cross-test claims\\n  are neither evaluated nor implied by the canary.\\n- **R8:** Mutation tests reject crossed bindings, checksum/fingerprint drift, unknown operators,\\n  Limit plus one, malformed closure, post-closure Evidence, stale run correlations, oversized HTTP\\n  messages, overlapping admission, cancellation leaks, and reuse after uncertain cleanup without\\n  partial success.\\n\\n## Early proof point\\n\\nBefore adding HTTP or the `testcore` adapter, generate the normal caller-closure protobuf contract\\nfrom Lean and prove that the Go interpreter returns the same detailed Run Evaluation statuses and\\nstable semantic outcome as the existing Lean checker for both normal and duplicate-delivery canned\\nEvidence. If parity cannot be established with the closed IR, the spec stops there rather than\\nadding test-harness or resident-process machinery around an untrusted evaluator.\\n\\n## Boundaries\\n<!-- scope: business -->\\n\\n- No production canary deployment, fleet scheduler, lease system, persistent queue, crash recovery,\\n  checkpoint/resume controller, release decision, Claim Assessment, or automatic promotion.\\n- No arbitrary code, dynamic checker, model registry, Lean installation, or model source in the\\n  resident Go executor.\\n- No whole-world verdict. The executor decides only the exact admitted Test under its bundled\\n  Evidence policy, Limits, Known Gaps, and bindings.\\n- No replacement of specialized unit, race, persistence, schema, authorization, or performance\\n  tests.\\n\\n## Decision Context\\n<!-- scope: both -->\\n\\n### Motivation\\n<!-- scope: business -->\\n\\nPrecompiling the semantic checks makes canary execution autonomous while preserving Lean as the\\nonly behavioral authority. A resident executor amortizes process and cluster startup and supports\\nEvidence that arrives after the workload has completed.\\n\\n### Implementation Tradeoffs\\n<!-- scope: technical -->\\n\\nA declarative protobuf interpreter adds a small trusted Go kernel and a versioned IR, but avoids\\nper-Test compilation, code injection, and deployment churn. Generated Go assertion code was rejected\\nbecause every contract change would require rebuilding the canary. Shipping Lean or WebAssembly was\\nrejected because canary has no Lean runtime and would inherit a much larger runtime/toolchain trust\\nsurface. Hard-coded checker profiles were rejected because the current caller-closure specialization\\ndoes not scale beyond one Test.\\n\\nUsing canonical ProtoJSON as the build-time handoff lets Lean own semantic lowering while generated\\nGo protobuf code owns only wire validation and deterministic binary encoding. The canonical runtime\\nartifact remains protobuf bytes; the intermediate JSON is not a second semantic source.\\n\\n## References\\n\\n- `.plans/UMPIRE4_SPEC.md` — authoritative model, Artifact,
